_comment: The one source of the guards' rule text. A denial is do + how + why; the session context lists the `do` of each rule in context.all (both hosts) and context.claudeWindows (Claude Code on Windows).

add.do: Stage the paths you created or changed by name: `git add <path>...`.
add.why: `git add -A`, `--all` and `.` also stage files you did not touch: the user's work in progress, other sessions' changes, generated files.

commit.do: Stage the paths you created or changed by name with `git add <path>...`, then run `git commit` without `-a`.
commit.why: `-a` also commits every tracked change you did not make.

chezmoi.do: Give `chezmoi apply --force` a target: `chezmoi apply --force <target>`, one drifted target at a time.
chezmoi.how: For each drifted target in `chezmoi status`, run `chezmoi diff <target>` first.
chezmoi.why: `apply --force` with no target overwrites every drifted file, including local edits nobody has reviewed.

kill.do: Stop a process by its PID: `kill <pid>`, `Stop-Process -Id <pid>` or `taskkill /PID <pid>`, after finding and checking the PID.
kill.how: Find it with `pgrep -af <pattern>` or, in PowerShell, `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "CommandLine LIKE '%<pattern>%'" | Select-Object ProcessId, CommandLine`, and check that the command line is the process you mean.
kill.why: Killing by name (`taskkill /IM`, `pkill`, `killall`, `Stop-Process -Name`) stops every process with that name, including the user's own and other sessions'.

rewrite.do: On Windows, a Bash command containing `\\` is written to a file and run from there (`source <file>`), so its backslashes reach bash as typed.

backslash.do: Write the program or text to a file with the Write tool, then run or pass it by path (`python <file>`, `bash <file>`, `--body-file <file>`).
backslash.why: On Windows the Bash tool turns every `\\` in a command into `\` before bash runs it, inside single quotes and quoted heredocs too, so this command would not run as written.

heredoc.do: In the PowerShell tool, write a multi-line string as a here-string: `@'`, the text, then `'@` at column 0 on its own line.
heredoc.how: For a longer program, write it to a file with the Write tool and run it by path (`pwsh -NoProfile -File <file>`). To use a bash heredoc, send the command to the Bash tool instead.
heredoc.why: PowerShell has no bash heredoc (`<<EOF`, `<<'EOF'`), so this command would not run as written.
